title_en: Homily on the Resurrection of the Lord
author: Amphilochius of Iconium
occasion: A festal homily for Easter, celebrating Christ's resurrection and urging the congregation to respond with thanksgiving, moral renewal, and shared joy.
argument: The homily proclaims Easter as the day of joy, salvation, and renewal, when Christ raised humanity from sin and death, opened paradise, and gave his life-giving body and blood as a ransom. The preacher calls the congregation to respond with gratitude, worship, and moral purification, offering hymns and virtues to God. He then invites all people, regardless of status or fasting practice, to share in the feast, because Christ the Passover has been sacrificed and the table is full. The homily celebrates Christ's victory over Hades and death, quoting Isaiah and Paul, and ends with a doxology to Christ as the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.

outline.move: The preacher announces the joy of Easter and describes Christ's saving work, then asks what return can be made and urges thanksgiving, worship, and moral purification.
The preacher invites all people to share in the feast, proclaims Christ's victory over Hades and death, and closes with a doxology.
The preacher repeats the announcement of Easter joy and Christ's saving work, and again urges thanksgiving, worship, and moral renewal, ending with a Psalm quotation rather than a doxology.
The preacher repeats the invitation to the feast, celebrates Christ's victory over Hades and death, and closes with a doxology.

scripture: The author quotes the Septuagint (LXX) and Pauline epistles. Psalm numbering follows the LXX. Citations should be given in modern form, e.g., Psalm 46:3 LXX (Psalm 47:2 Hebrew) for 'the Lord most high is awesome, a great king over all the earth'; 1 Corinthians 5:7 for 'Christ our Passover has been sacrificed'; 1 Corinthians 15:55 for 'O death, where is your sting? O Hades, where is your victory?'; 1 Corinthians 15:20 for 'Christ, risen from the dead, has become the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.'
uncertain: The exact date of composition within Amphilochius' career is uncertain.
The precise liturgical setting beyond Easter is not specified in the text.
The relationship between the repeated sections (u01-open, u01-rem-mid) and the early/close sections is unclear; they may represent overlapping versions or a composite text.

_unresolved_facts.claim: The preacher calls the congregation to respond with gratitude, worship, and moral purification, offering hymns and virtues to God. He then invites all people, regardless of status or fasting practice, to share in the feast
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: u01-open: εὐχαριστήσωμεν καὶ προσπέσωμεν τῷ κυρίῳ καὶ προσκυνήσωμεν αὐτῷ, καὶ προσφέρωμεν τὰ μῦρα καὶ τοὺς ὕμνους ὡς δῶρα μετὰ φόβου καὶ εὐλαβείας... ἀγαπήσωμεν... ἀποθάνωμεν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ἀποθανόντος ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν δωρεάν, πορευθῶμεν ὀπίσω τῶν ἁγίων αὐτοῦ ἐντολῶν; u01-rem-early: ἀπολαύσωμεν πάντες... εἰσέλθωμεν χαίροντες εἰς τὴν χαρὰν τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν
_unresolved_facts.fix: The argument reverses the actual order: in the source, the invitation to all people to share in the feast (u01-rem-early) comes BEFORE the call to thanksgiving, worship, and moral purification (u01-open, u01-rem-mid). The brief's 'He then' implies chronological sequence that doesn't match the section order.

_unresolved_facts.claim: u01-rem-early: 'The preacher invites all people to share in the feast, proclaims Christ's victory over Hades and death, and closes with a doxology.'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: u01-rem-early ends: Χριστὸς ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστὰς ἀπαρχὴ τῶν κεκοιμημένων ἐγένετο· αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος καὶ ἡ προσκύνησις καὶ ἡ μεγαλοσύνη νῦν καὶ ἀεὶ καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. ἀμήν.
_unresolved_facts.fix: u01-rem-early does close with a doxology, but the outline should note that this section also contains the Isaiah quotation and the 'O death, where is your sting' passage, not just 'victory over Hades and death' generally.

_unresolved_facts.claim: u01-rem-mid: 'ending with a Psalm quotation rather than a doxology'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: u01-rem-mid ends: «κύριος ὕψιστος φοβερὸς βασιλεὺς ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν «.
_unresolved_facts.fix: u01-rem-mid does end with a Psalm quotation (Psalm 46:3 LXX), but the outline should clarify that this section is incomplete—it cuts off mid-homily and does not contain the feast invitation or Hades victory narrative that complete the pattern seen in other sections.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Isaiah (quoted prophecy): 'introduced by 'as Isaiah foretold' and quoted directly'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: u01-rem-early: καθὼς Ἡσαΐας προεῖπεν· ἐπικράνθη ὁ Ἅιδης συναντήσας σοι κάτω; u01-rem-close: καθὼς Ἡσαΐας προανεφώνησεν «ὁ Ἅιδης « λέγων «ἐπικράνθη συναντήσας σοι κάτω «
_unresolved_facts.fix: In u01-rem-early, Isaiah is introduced with προεῖπεν ('foretold') but the quotation is not marked with quotation marks; in u01-rem-close, the introduction uses προανεφώνησεν ('proclaimed beforehand') and the quotation is marked with quotation marks. The 'how_marked' field should distinguish these differences.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Scripture (mixed quotations): 'marked by quotation marks in the source; includes Pauline and Psalm texts woven together'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: u01-rem-close contains: «μέγας κύριος...», «τὸ πάσχα ἡμῶν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἐτύθη Χριστός «, «γεύσασθε καὶ ἴδετε ὅτι χρηστὸς ὁ κύριος «, «ὁ Ἅιδης « λέγων «ἐπικράνθη συναντήσας σοι κάτω «, «ἥρπασεν ὡς λέων «, «ποῦ σου, θάνατε, τὸ κέντρον; ποῦ σου, Ἅιδη, τὸ νῖκος; «, «Χριστὸς ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστὰς ἀπαρχὴ τῶν κεκοιμημένων ἐγένετο «
_unresolved_facts.fix: The quotation marks in the source are inconsistent and partial—some phrases have opening marks only, some have both, some are nested oddly. The brief should not imply systematic quotation marking. Also, u01-rem-early has NO quotation marks for Isaiah or Paul, while u01-open has none at all.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Christ: source_forms include 'Χριστὸς ὁ θεὸς', 'Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: u01-rem-early: ἔσωσε γὰρ ἡμᾶς Χριστὸς ὁ θεὸς; u01-rem-close: θεὸς Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ὃς καὶ ἐπέφανεν ἡμῖν
_unresolved_facts.fix: The source forms are correct but incomplete: 'Χριστὸς ὁ θεὸς' appears in u01-rem-early, and 'θεὸς Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς' appears in u01-rem-close. However, 'Χριστὸς ὁ κύριος' also appears (u01-rem-early: θεὸς κύριος καὶ ἐπέφανεν ἡμῖν; u01-rem-close: γεύσασθε καὶ ἴδετε ὅτι χρηστὸς ὁ κύριος—though this is a variant of Psalm 33:9 LXX).

_unresolved_facts.source_quote: The source uses both 'ὁ ᾅδης'/'ὁ Ἅιδης' (Hades, the underworld personified) and 'ὁ θάνατος' (death). They are closely related but distinct: e.g., u01-rem-early: κατέπιεν ὁ θάνατος ἀγνοῶν... κατέπιε ζωήν, κατεπόθη ὑπὸ τῆς ζωῆς; u01-rem-close: κατέπιεν ὁ θάνατος ἀγνοῶν, καταπιὼν δὲ ἔγνω ὃν κατέπιε
_unresolved_facts.fix: The brief should note that 'death' (θάνατος) appears as a parallel/alternate personification alongside Hades, particularly in the swallowing/being swallowed motif. The names field should include 'Death' or the brief should clarify that θάνατος is treated as a distinct actor in the drama.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Psalm 46:3 LXX (Psalm 47:2 Hebrew) for 'the Lord most high is awesome, a great king over all the earth'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: u01-open: ὅτι κύριος ὕψιστος φοβερὸς βασιλεὺς ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν; u01-rem-mid: ὅτι «κύριος ὕψιστος φοβερὸς βασιλεὺς ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν «; u01-rem-close: [not present, section ends before this point]
_unresolved_facts.fix: The citation is Psalm 46:3 LXX / Psalm 47:2 Hebrew, but the source text reads 'κύριος ὕψιστος φοβερὸς βασιλεὺς ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν' which matches Psalm 46:3 LXX (ὅτι κύριος ὕψιστος, φοβερός, βασιλεὺς μέγας ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν). However, the brief's 'Psalm 47:2 Hebrew' is imprecise—Hebrew verse numbering would be Psalm 47:3 MT. More importantly, the source lacks 'μέγας' before 'βασιλεύς' in u01-open and u01-rem-mid.

_unresolved_facts.claim: 1 Corinthians 5:7 for 'Christ our Passover has been sacrificed'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: u01-rem-early: ὅτι τὸ πάσχα ἡμῶν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἐτύθη Χριστός; u01-rem-close: ὅτι «τὸ πάσχα ἡμῶν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἐτύθη Χριστός «
_unresolved_facts.fix: The source has 'τὸ πάσχα ἡμῶν... ἐτύθη Χριστός' (Christ is the predicate, not the subject of 'sacrificed'), which differs from 1 Cor 5:7 LXX/NA28: τὸ πάσχα ἡμῶν ἐτύθη Χριστός—actually this matches. But the brief should note the variant word order in u01-rem-close with quotation marks.
